newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Korea's Tong Yang in $200 mln Cambodian venture.
newsitem.headline: Korea's Tong Yang in $200 mln Cambodian venture.

text.p: South Korea's Tong Yang Group on Friday announced a $200 million joint venture with a Cambodian firm to develop a cement plant in southern Cambodia.

Tong Yang and a local partner Khaou Chuly Development Company Ltd have obtained a 30-year lease to a limestone quarry and permits to build a cement plant that will produce up to 820,000 tonnes per year, company and government officials said at a signing ceremony with the Industry Ministry.
They said Tong Yang, with an 85 percent stake and Khaou Chuly, with a 15 percent stake, would begin constructing in 1998 and open the plant -- to be the biggest in Cambodia -- by the year 2000.
The cement plant will be located in the southern province of Kampot. The output will mainly supply the Cambodian market, which uses about one million tonnes per year.
Most cement in Cambodia is currently imported, said Minister of Industry Pou Sothirak.
South Korea opened a trade office in Cambodia last year. There are 13 other South Korean companies in Cambodia totalling $12 million in investmnent.
